newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ government still eyeing property sales - Birch.
newsitem.headline: NZ government still eyeing property sales - Birch.

text.p: WELLINGTON, March 19 (Reuter) The New Zealand government plans to continue to sell properties in Government Property Services' (GPS) portfolio, Finance Minister Bill Birch said on Wednesday.

"The coalition govenment doesn't think the ownership of commercial buildings is part of the strategic role of government. It is a collection of buildings. We will work to eventually reduce the ownership of the buildings which we don't think are strategic, " Birch told Reuters in an interview.
A planned sale of the bulk of GPS properties, excluding some buildings housing key government and defence functions, was put on hold last year after prices did not meet expectations.
"We think the money is better off in debt repayment, quite frankly," Birch said.
He said no decision had been made on whether the properties would be sold as a whole portfolio or individually.
He said he had not had a chance to talk to the GPS board since the election, but "that choice is still there...It is a market decision at a particular time."
He indicated there could be sales of other assets not included in the coalition government's list of strategic assets.
Birch said national grid operator Transpower's spur lines were a sensitive issue because they were part of a strategic asset.
"But clearly we expect Transpower to manage its business to enhance shareholding value and there will be issues around particular assets.
"No board decision has been made, other than that we don't sell Transpower. It would be a question of how central to Transpower this particular asset is businesswise."
Spur lines are those that branch off the main grid and feed a small number of power stations.

Birch said state-owned television channel TV2 was not on the coalition's list of strategic assets, but there were a number of policy decisions to made before the shape of broadcasting could be finalised, and this was likely to take place before July.
